doc.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys Tier List
doc.summary: The Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list, updated October 30, 2026: Blitzclique and Angelechy lead Tier 1. Ranked from 43,069 YGO Omega ladder matches.

infobox.caption: Surge Blitzclique, the most used card of the top deck

blocks.md: This Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list ranks the strongest decks on the YGO Omega Genesys ladder by their results, using data through October 29, 2026. **Blitzclique** (4.5% of the meta, 60.7% wins) and **Angelechy** (3.3% of the meta, 60.4% wins) share Tier 1.

blocks.caption: The Genesys tier list at a glance

blocks.md: A tier here measures **how well a deck wins**, not how much it is played, and a small sample can't lift a deck to the top. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-october-30-2026); for the other ladder, the [TCG tier list](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-tcg-tier-list); for the numbers as they change, the [live statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys).

blocks.text: Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list at a glance

blocks.md:
| | |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | Blitzclique, Angelechy |
| Tier 1.5 | None |
| Tier 2 | Angelechy / Ashtra, Artmage, Centur-Ion / Angelechy |
| Decks in the tiers | 22 |
| Matches counted | 43,069 |
| Players | 4,927 |
| Going first wins | 56.8% |
| Season opened | September 20, 2026 |

The Genesys ladder is 40 days into the 09.2026 season, with 43,069 matches from 4,927 players. The most played deck, Blitzclique, holds 4.5% of the meta, and the 22 decks in these tiers cover 29% of it. New to the format? The [format primer](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-formats) explains the 100-point rule.

Blitzclique has the best score on the ladder, with 60.7% wins over 9,306 deck-games. It wins 70.5% going first and 52.1% going second. Its share rose 0.1 points over the last 7 days.

Win rates here run from 59.7% (Centur-Ion / Angelechy) to 59.9% (Angelechy / Ashtra).

blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
Popularity and results don't always agree. The underplayed decks reach Tier 2 or better on a small share of the meta, though the people playing them may be specialists, so treat them as leads to test. The overplayed decks are among the ten most played without reaching Tier 2.

- **Underplayed:** Centur-Ion / Angelechy (0.6% of the meta, 59.7% wins), Artmage (0.7% of the meta, 59.9% wins) and Angelechy / Ashtra (0.8% of the meta, 59.9% wins)
- **Overplayed:** Hecahands (2.6% of the meta, 54.0% wins), HERO (2.3% of the meta, 50.2% wins) and Dragon Ruler (2.3% of the meta, 50.5% wins)

Best and worst matchup for each top deck against Tiers 1 to 3. A matchup is listed only when its whole 95% confidence interval sits on one side of 50%, with at least 80 games.

| Deck | Best matchup | Worst matchup |
|---|---|---|
| **Blitzclique** | **[Angelechy, 56.0% (389 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | None clear |
| **Angelechy** | None clear | **[Blitzclique, 44.0% (389 games)]{#ff8594}** |
| **Angelechy / Ashtra** | None clear | None clear |
| **Artmage** | None clear | None clear |
| **Centur-Ion / Angelechy** | None clear | None clear |
| **White Forest / Angelechy** | None clear | None clear |

Generic Main Deck cards seen across at least two archetypes, by share of deck-games. [Skull Meister](/wiki/card/67750322) shows up in 28.4% of decks, and [Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit](/wiki/card/59438930) shows up in 27.1% of decks.

Every number comes from ranked matches played on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data behind our [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys). Nothing is voted on or picked by hand.

These are **power tiers**: they rank results. The tiers on the statistics page measure something else, how much a deck is played, so the same deck can sit in different tiers on the two pages.

**Each deck gets a score, the Wilson lower bound of its win rate.** That is the low end of the range its true win rate is likely in, so a deck needs both a good record and enough games to score well: 60% over 500 games scores below 58% over 5,000. A tier is how far a deck's score sits below the best deck on the ladder:

| Tier | Points below the best score |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | Up to 1, the best 2 decks only |
| Tier 1.5 | Up to 1, every other deck |
| Tier 2 | 1 to 3 |
| Tier 3 | 3 to 6 |
| Tier 4 | 6 to 9 |

The best deck is always Tier 1. Decks past the last band stay outside the tiers. A deck needs at least 0.5% of the meta and 10 players to be ranked at all, because the score corrects for few games, not for few pilots.

- **Meta share** is the deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, and mirror matches count.
- **Win rate** leaves mirror matches out, because a mirror always wins exactly half. The ± is its 95% confidence interval.
- **Decks** are grouped by the archetypes they run, so a hybrid counts apart from pure builds.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: This is ladder play on a simulator, not tournament results. Players of every level are in it, and a deck played mostly by specialists can score above what it would do in most hands. It shows what wins on the ladder, which is not always what wins a premier event.

items.q: What is the best Genesys deck right now?
items.md: Blitzclique, with a 60.7% win rate at 4.5% of the meta. It has the strongest win rate once sample size is counted.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It comes from ranked ladder matches on YGO Omega. That gives a far larger sample than tournaments, but it reflects ladder play, not premier events.

By score: the Wilson lower bound of a deck's win rate, which rewards a good record over many games. Tiers 1 to 4 are up to 1, 3, 6, 9 points below the best deck. Tier 1 holds 2 decks at most, and any other deck that close goes to Tier 1.5. Decks under 0.5% of the meta or 10 players aren't ranked.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. Tiers follow results. Hecahands holds 2.6% of the meta and sits in Tier 4, while Centur-Ion / Angelechy holds 0.6% and sits in Tier 2.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: Going first wins 56.8% of games on the Genesys ladder.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-october-30-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) shows the current numbers between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
